title: fix(deps): re-lock @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, follow-redirects, launch-editor and vite onto their fixed releases
body:
Fixes #25041

Clause-②: no

## What this does

`main`'s scheduled `Validate Dependencies` run 39536495453 is red at its OSV step: the lockfile matches 12 advisory rows (9 distinct ids, 6 High) in four locked packages, and every one names a fixed release. Every declared range on every path already admits its fix, so this is a **re-lock only**. `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the whole diff. It adds no override, no `osv-scanner.toml` exemption, and no `package.json` range.

| Package | Locked → resolved | Advisories | Path (`pnpm why -r`) | How |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` | 1.31.0 → **1.32.1** (fix 1.32.0) | GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw, GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453, GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw, GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq | direct `^1.30.1` in `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/connector-mcp` and the private `@objectstack/example-showcase` | re-lock |
| `follow-redirects` | 1.16.0 → **1.16.1** | GHSA-8r9p-f939-6h3c, GHSA-q3jh-wrc6-jgq8 | `mongodb-memory-server-core@11.3.0` (`^1.16.0`) ← `mongodb-memory-server` ← `@objectstack/driver-mongodb` devDependencies | re-lock |
| `launch-editor` | 2.14.1 → **2.14.2** | GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm, GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv, GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw | `@changesets/cli@3.0.3` (`^2.14.1`) ← the root devDependencies | re-lock |
| `vite` | 8.0.16 → **8.3.4** (fixed lines 8.1.6 / 8.2.4 / 8.3.3) | the same three as `launch-editor` (vite bundles it) | `vitest@4.1.11` (dependency and peer `^6.0.0 \|\| ^7.0.0 \|\| ^8.0.0`), `@vitest/mocker@4.1.11` (peer, same range), `fumadocs-mdx@15.2.3` (optional peer `7.x.x \|\| 8.x.x`) | re-lock |

**Each target is the newest release inside the existing ranges.** That is what a targeted `pnpm update` resolves, and what a fresh downstream install gets. For `vite`, the three fixed lines come from the advisories' own ranges in the OSV npm database: introduced 8.0.0 fixed 8.1.6, introduced 8.2.0 fixed 8.2.4, introduced 8.3.0 fixed 8.3.3. 8.3.4 sits outside all three. `vitest@4.1.11`'s peer range admits it, and so does its own devDependency: both `vitest` 4.1.11 and `fumadocs-mdx` 15.2.3 develop against `vite ^8.2.0`, so 8.1.6 would sit below what either consumer tests against. If 8.3.4 ever has to be backed off, 8.2.4 is the fix on that line.

## How the lockfile was moved, and the route rejected first

- **Rejected: a targeted `pnpm update`.** Measured twice, with `--no-save`, so no `package.json` moved:
  - The first spelling was `pnpm update -r --depth Infinity --no-save follow-redirects launch-editor vite @modelcontextprotocol/sdk`. It moved the SDK alone, leaving `follow-redirects`, `launch-editor` and `vite` exactly where they were.
  - The same run moved 12 unrelated packages, at +101/−68 lines: `@inquirer/ansi` / `confirm` / `core` / `type`, `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime` 1.2.4 → 1.2.5, `node-abi` 3.96.0 → 3.99.0, and `seroval` / `seroval-plugins` 1.6.8 → 1.6.11. It also added new copies of `@babel/runtime`, `ip-address`, `nanoid`, `postcss` and `set-cookie-parser`, and touched the `knex`, `tsup` and `postcss-load-config` snapshots.
  - `pnpm update -r --no-save @modelcontextprotocol/sdk` alone, at default depth, produced the identical churn.
  - Control: a plain non-frozen `pnpm install` on the base lockfile leaves 0 changed files, so the churn is `update`'s own.
- **Taken: the precedent's recipe (#21951).** I appended four temporary exact overrides to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and ran `pnpm install`. I then restored the file to its HEAD blob and ran `pnpm install` again. The second install keeps the four resolutions, because every declared range admits them.
  - The restore is proven, not assumed: `git hash-object pnpm-workspace.yaml` equals the HEAD blob `ecbd0f4bfdeb4c7c03bb43d910c5f2406fbadea7`, and `git diff HEAD` on it is empty.
  - The lockfile's own `overrides:` section is unchanged, and no importer specifier moved.

## Lockfile diff scope

`pnpm-lock.yaml` only, **+187/−237**. The `packages:` section goes from 1372 to 1367 keys, with 26 removed and 21 added. Every moved entry belongs to the four packages or to `vite`'s own closure:

- the four rows in the table above;
- `rolldown` 1.0.3 → 1.2.14 (`vite` 8.3.4 declares `~1.2.12`), its 14 platform bindings 1.0.3 → 1.2.14, the new `@rolldown/binding-android-arm-eabi` 1.2.14, and `@oxc-project/types` 0.133.0 → 0.154.0;
- **dropped**: `@rolldown/binding-wasm32-wasi` 1.0.3 and the chain only it reached. That chain is `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime` 1.2.4, `@emnapi/core` 1.10.0, `@emnapi/runtime` 1.10.0, `@emnapi/wasi-threads` 1.2.1 and `@tybys/wasm-util` 0.10.4.
  - `npm view rolldown@1.2.14 optionalDependencies` declares no wasm32-wasi binding, while 1.0.3 declares one.
  - `@emnapi/runtime` 1.11.3 stays, because it is the copy `@img/sharp-wasm32` already used on the base.

The `snapshots:` section goes from 1379 to 1374 keys, covering the same names plus the peer-suffix rewrites on `vitest`, `@vitest/mocker` and `fumadocs-mdx`. In the importers section, 3 lines move the SDK version and 80 version strings carry the new `vite`/`rolldown` peer suffix (79 `vitest`, 1 `fumadocs-mdx`). Nothing else moved.

## Local proofs, at `7b0295c723`

| Proof | Exit | Reading |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | 0 | |
| `pnpm check:vendor-export-contract-resolve` | 0 | `VERDICT: PASS — vendor export contract (registry resolution, installed with npm@11.21.0), 3 edge(s) verified`. It governs only the better-auth family, so it passes over the SDK without judging it. |
| `pnpm check:override-consistency` | 0 | `9 published-manifest declaration(s) … all resolve to their override targets` |
| `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/mcp --filter=@objectstack/connector-mcp --concurrency=2` (shared verify lock) | 0 | `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 33/33 tasks, 0 cached |
| `test` for both packages (shared verify lock) | 0 | `@objectstack/mcp` 40 files / 479 tests passed; `@objectstack/connector-mcp` 4 files / 36 tests passed |
| `typecheck` for both packages (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck`) | 0 | both test layers compile at their existing ledger counts (mcp 6 files / 53 errors / 8 pinned signatures; connector-mcp 1 / 5 / 1) |

- **The vite consumer** is those two vitest runs. Resolved from each package, `vitest` 4.1.11 loads `vite` 8.3.4, and the installed SDK is 1.32.1.
- **The docs build was not run**, because it would prove nothing about this change. `apps/docs` builds through Next, and `fumadocs-mdx` touches `vite` only in its `dist/vite` plugin entry and `rolldown` only in its type declarations. CI's `Build Docs` runs the production command.

## OSV reading

I measured with OSV-Scanner **2.5.0**, the binary the workflow's pinned action image ships. Its sha256 `edcfc41d…524e0c` matches the release's `SHA256SUMS`. `api.osv.dev` answers 403 from this container, so the scan ran offline (`--offline-vulnerabilities --download-offline-databases`) against the npm database downloaded 2026-10-21 03:59 UTC. Each side ran under its own `osv-scanner.toml`, with the identical invocation.

- **Base `dfe60e3a0c`: exit 1.** The 12 rows are byte-for-byte the scheduled run's, with the sprintf-js exemption filtered.
- **This PR `7b0295c723`: exit 0, `No issues found`.** The sprintf-js exemption is filtered here too. That is the control that shows the database loaded and matched.
- **`scripts/osv-base-relative.mjs`** over both JSON results exits 0: `0 introduced, 0 inherited, 9 resolved`.
- **One void reading, declared:** a first head scan without `--download-offline-databases` printed `No issues found` at exit 0 with no `Loaded npm local db` line, reading the exemption as unused. It had loaded no database, and it is not counted.

What closes the card is the next scheduled (or a `workflow_dispatch`) `Validate Dependencies` run on `main`. This PR's own run takes the base-relative path.

## Changeset: `skip-changeset`, measured

Nothing publishes. No `package.json` changed, so every published package's declared ranges are byte-identical and a downstream install resolves exactly as before.

- **The two published consumers do not bundle the SDK.** `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/connector-mcp` (`files: ["dist", …]`) keep it as an external import: 4 and 3 `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/…` import specifiers remain in their built `dist`. The SDK's own `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "…"` definition appears in 0 of their `dist` files. The positive control is 6 hits in the SDK's own `dist`.
- **No built `dist` names the other moved packages.** None of the 33 built `dist` trees names `rolldown`, `launch-editor` or `follow-redirects`, while `vite`'s own `dist` does, which is the control.
- **The other three are dev-only paths.** They arrive only through devDependencies (`driver-mongodb`, the root, `vitest`) and the private docs app.

## Gates

- **Derivation.** I ran `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `7b0295c723`, which derived 19 commands from 1 path. I ran all 19, each exit captured before any pipe.
- **`--ran` reconciliation:** `19 derived, 18 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- **18 exited 0:** `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-closing-keyword-parity` (+ `--self-test`), `check-comment-mask-corpus`, `check-dts-emitted --self-test`, `check-osv-exemptions` (+ `--self-test`), `osv-base-relative --self-test`, and the `pnpm` gates `check:driver-memory-census`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:gitlink-declared`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:override-consistency`, `check:refd-timer-probe`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`, `check:vendor-export-contract-resolve` and `check:watch-hint-literal`.
- **Partial sweeps:** `check:dts-closure` and `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` swept the 33 built packages only.
- **NOT MEASURED:** `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, needs a full `pnpm build`). CI's `Build Core` and `Lint & Repo Gates` measure it on the built tree.
- **`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`** (`origin/main` = `eddffc3390`): exit 0, clean. `pnpm-lock.yaml` is not routed to the `os-regen` driver, so this local reading answers GitHub's question. The 2 commits `main` gained since the base touch none of `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the root `package.json` or `osv-scanner.toml`.

## Acceptance notes

- `vite` moves three minors, 8.0.16 → 8.3.4, and `rolldown` 1.0.3 → 1.2.14 with it. Every vitest suite in the repo runs on this pair, so CI's `Test Core` is the wide reading. Locally, only the two MCP packages' 515 tests ran.
- In this workspace, `pnpm update` (even depth 0, one direct dependency) re-resolves a fixed set of unrelated packages, and with `--depth Infinity` it does not move the transitive targets at all. The temporary-override re-lock is the route that keeps a lockfile refresh narrow here. Class: none (tooling behaviour, not a defect of this repo); carrier: none.
- A local offline OSV scan without `--download-offline-databases` can read green having loaded no database. Read the `Loaded npm local db` line, or an exemption reading as filtered, before trusting a local "No issues found".
- `pnpm install` prints `ioredis-mock 8.13.1: unmet peer ioredis@^5: found 6.0.0`. That warning is already on `main`, and this diff does not cause it.
